newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's opposition leaders abandon rally plan.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's opposition leaders abandon rally plan.

text.p: Kenya's two leading opposition politicians pulled back from an earlier declaration on Tuesday that they would organise "illegal" rallies to press for constitutional reforms before elections later this year.

Raila Odinga and Kenneth Matiba of the opposition National Development Party (NDP) and Ford-Asili parties respectively were reported by privately-owned Kenya Television Network (KTN) as saying the they would seek dialogue with government instead.
The two said nation-wide rallies called for June 21 would also coincide with the installation of the Catholic archbishop of Nairobi.
"We called for the rallies and we have now reconsidered. We remain open to dialogue with the government," Odinga told the news conference attended by Matiba.
He added: "We do not want confrontation to take place across the country."
The government of President Daniel arap Moi had outlawed the rallies and Moi had vowed to use all resources at his disposal to stop the rallies from going ahead.

Two weeks ago, security forces broke up an opposition-Church rally declared illegal by the government, sparking two days of rioting in the capital that left one person dead and scores of shops and stalls looted.
KTN also reported a statement from the western donor community urging for dialogue between government and the opposition in the run-up to elections.

"We call on both the government and those organisations advocating reforms to engage in dialogue, aimed at reaching compromise rather than confrontation," said the joint statement signed by representatives of western missions.
Moi, aged 73 and in power since 1978, must call elections in 1997 pitting the ruling KANU party against an opposition fractured along ethnic and personal lines.
The opposition wants the review or repeal of six laws including the Public Order Act, reviled as an instrument of suppression. It is also demanding greater access to state-controlled media.
